info.name: avoid-pp gateway (C07)
info.description:
Health, readiness and request-id behaviour for the avoid-pp gateway at C07.

Start the server first:

    AVOIDPP_DETECTOR_URL=http://localhost:9000 AVOIDPP_ADDR=:8099 go run ./gateway/cmd/server

The collection uses port 8099 because nginx occupies the gateway's default 8080 on this machine. Change the {{baseUrl}} collection variable if yours is free.

There is no scan endpoint yet - that arrives at C09. The 'Scan endpoint' request asserts a 404 on purpose: a route that exists but does nothing is indistinguishable from protection that silently fails open.

request.description: Answers 200 whenever the process is running, regardless of initialisation. Makes NO external call: a probe that reaches a model provider bills on every scrape and reports the process dead whenever that provider wobbles.

item.name: 2. Readiness - can it serve traffic now?

request.description:
A different question from liveness. Failing readiness means 'route traffic away but leave the process alone'; failing liveness means 'restart it'. Merging the two causes a classic outage: a server waiting on a dependency reports itself dead, gets killed, restarts, waits again.

Returns 503 'not_ready' during startup and while draining.

item.name: 3. Scan endpoint - must NOT exist yet

request.description:
This is a real, contract-valid scan request (a Finnish passage with an embedded Dutch instruction). At C07 it must 404.

That is deliberate. A registered route that returns nothing looks exactly like protection that silently fails open. The endpoint appears at C09, when it has behaviour.

exec: pm.test('404 - endpoint not implemented until C09', () => pm.response.to.have.status(404));
pm.test('does NOT return an allow decision', () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.include('allow'));

item.name: 4. Request id - caller's id is propagated

request.description: A safe inbound id is reused so a caller's own correlation id survives the gateway boundary.

item.name: 5. Request id - unsafe id is replaced, not sanitised

request.description:
An inbound id is attacker-controlled and reaches logs, so anything outside the contract's 64-char bound and a conservative charset is REPLACED rather than cleaned up.

Replaced, not sanitised, on purpose: a rewritten id would no longer match the caller's own records, which defeats the point silently. Same handling applies to newlines (log injection), control characters and ANSI escapes.

exec: pm.test('over-long id was NOT reused', () => pm.expect(got).to.not.eql(sent));
pm.test('a fresh id was issued instead', () => pm.expect(got).to.be.a('string').and.not.empty);
pm.test('replacement respects the 64-char contract bound', () => pm.expect(got.length).to.be.at.most(64));
pm.test('not a truncation of the input', () => pm.expect(sent.startsWith(got)).to.be.false);
